title: findings@2
description: Judge-boundary successor to findings@1, from the retro after RUN-5. Declared on review fanout steps ONLY, never on reconcile: the builtin `aggregate` carries through only the input element's own keys, so a schema requiring `id` on the aggregate document makes the §7.6 E5 conjunction unsatisfiable and V30 refuses the workflow at register time — findings@1 remains the reconcile document for exactly that reason. This version requires the canonical anchor keys after RUN-5 recorded 7 judge-architecture findings keyed `location`/`rule` instead of `file`/`id`/`line`, which anything downstream keyed on `id` silently dropped. Under this document a malformed judge payload refuses at that judge's own `complete`, with per-judge attribution, instead of vanishing later. Aggregate-only properties (`members`, `held`, `demoted_from`, `operator_resolved`) are removed — judges never emit them and the aggregate never validates against this document.

id.description: Stable identifier for the finding, unique within the payload. Required here, unlike findings@1: this document is never declared on the aggregate step, so the V30 concern that kept `id` optional there does not apply.

severity.description: The finding's severity, on 02 §6's five-value ladder. The enum's document order IS the order thresholds compare on (`any(severity >= high)`): info < low < medium < high < blocker. Judges author on the general or security ladder fragment and map onto these values at emit time.

file.description: Repo-relative path the finding is anchored to. Required: an unanchored finding cannot be clustered by locus or acted on by fix.

evidence.description: What a skeptic can re-run or re-read to confirm the finding.

alternative.description: A concrete alternative to the flagged approach. Optional at every severity (see findings@1's note on DKT-51).
